reconciliation_notes: CORRECTED one load-bearing field vs authored: hbm_bandwidth_bps 1.31e13 (13.1 TB/s) -> 2.2e13 (22 TB/s). Both verifiers flag the authored 13 TB/s as a superseded pre-announcement estimate; the GTC2026 third-party consensus (Thunder Compute/Spheron/Barrack AI/VRLA Tech, 288GB HBM4 @ 22 TB/s, 10.8 GT/s/pin) is the current published figure. Adopted the higher-trust consensus value; confidence stays BRONZE (third_party only, no vendor datasheet PDF located). hbm_capacity_bytes kept at 3.09e11 (288 GiB binary, matching H100 twin binary convention) — verifier agrees on 288GB; flagged binary(3.09e11)/decimal(2.88e11) ambiguity, immaterial to experiments. compute_instances=224 SM kept (both verifiers: 3rd-party consensus, BRONZE not vendor). device_peak_flops_bf16 6.25e15 kept as directional estimate (honest range 5-13 PF; if 50PF NVFP4 is dense, BF16~12.5PF); per_instance_mac_s 1.395e13 = 6.25e15/2/224 recomputes exactly (verified 1.395e13*224*2=6.25e15). tdp_w kept at 1800 (Max-Q) with explicit Max-P 2300W range in meta. transistors_billion(336), process_node(N3P), nvlink6(3.6) are the only SILVER fields (multi-source press agreement); nvlink6 omitted from twin leaf per single-device convention. Twin structure = RB-05 backing HBM4 -> L2 -> per-SM shared(sram) -> compute mxu, single accelerator (1 Rubin package). OVERALL TIER = BRONZE: all three load-bearing fields (bandwidth_bps, capacity_bytes, device peak) are BRONZE, per spec twin=min(load-bearing). All estimate/SRAM/compute-leaf fields remain BRONZE directional-only per do-not-package-guesses-as-fact rule.
